questions.question:
56248. The main difference between interval and ratio variables is-
শ্রেণী ও আনুপাতিক চলকের প্রধান পার্থক্য হলো–
questions.option1: Interval has true zero; ratio does not, Interval এ True Zero থাকে; Ratio তে থাকে না
questions.option2: Ratio has true zero; interval does not, Ratio তে True Zero থাকে; Interval এ থাকে না
questions.option3: Both have true zero , দুটোতেই True Zero থাকে
questions.option4: Ratio variables cannot be measured, আনুপাতিক চলক মাপা যায় না
questions.explain:
Ratio has true zero while interval does not true zero

example- for ratio scale: Person's age is a ratio level of measurement. The difference between the ages 30 and 20 years is the same as the difference between 20 and 10 years. A person is zero when born. Again a 20-year-old is twice as old as a 10-year-old. Hence, all types of algebraic operations afe meaningful with ratio level of measurement.

for interval- Temperature is an interval level of measurement. The distance between 30°C (30 degree Celsius) and 32°C is the same as the distance between 70°C and 72°C. There is an agreed-on unit of measurement and an arbitrary zero point. A temperature of 0°C does not indicate the absence of temperature - there is still a temperature. Again, the equivalent readings of 40° and 80° in Celsius scale are 104° and 176° in Fahrenheit scale. Here, 80/40 = 2, and 176/104 =1.69; i.e., the ratios are different. Obviously, 80°C is never twice as 40°C. That is, multiplication or division in interval level of measurement is meaningless.

source- statistics and probabiliy: an introductory analysis by siddiqur rahman, fundamentals of probability and probability distribution by manindra kumar roy, statistics by Md abdul aziz

questions.question: 56243. Choose the correct sentence:
questions.option1: It is high time you making a decision.
questions.option2: It is high time you make a decision.
questions.option3: It is high time you made a decision.
questions.option4: It is high time you could make a decision.
questions.explain:
• Correct sentence: It is high time you made a decision.

• Use of It is time/ It is high time:
- It is time/ It is high time এরপর যদি subject থাকে তাহলে পরবর্তী verb টি past indefinite tense এ হয়।
- কোনো কিছু করার এখনই উপযুক্ত সময় অর্থে It is time/ It is high time ব্যবহৃত হয়।

- নিয়মানুযায়ী, প্রদত্ত বাক্যে It is high time এর পরে subject (you) আছে, তাই এর পরে verb এর past form (made) বসবে।

• More examples:
- It is high time she left the place.
- It is high time you started studying.

• তবে, It is time/It is high time এরপর যদি subject না থাকে তবে to + verb হয়।
- যেমন: It is high time to stop corruption.

অন্য অপশন বিশ্লেষণ-
ক) It is high time you making a decision.
→ ভুল, কারণ verb এর past form হবে।

খ) It is high time you make a decision.
→ ভুল, কারণ verb এর past form (made) হবে।

ঘ) It is high time you could make a decision.
→ ভুল, কারণ could make দ্বারা অতীতের কাজ বুঝানো হয়, কিন্তু It is high time দ্বারা বর্তমানের কাজ বুঝানো হয়।

Source:
1. A Passage to the English Language by S.M. Zakir Hussain.
2. Advanced Learner's Communicative English Grammar and Composition by Chowdhury and Hossain.

questions.question:
56238. If quartiles Q₁ = 20 and Q3 = 30, Which of the following must be true?
I. The median is 25.
II. The standard deviation is at least 10.
যদি প্রথম চতুর্থক = 20 এবং 3য় চতুর্থক =30 হয় তবে নিচের কোনটি অবশ্যই সত্য?
1- মধ্যমা 25
2- পরিমিত ব্যবধান কমপক্ষে 10
questions.explain:
explain: i) median could be any number between Q1,Q3. Say 22,25,27 etc.

ii)Standard deviation depends on how spread out the data are around the mean.

But an IQR of 10 does not force the standard deviation is to be ≥ 10.

Example: Data = {20, 25, 30}.

Here, Q₁ = 20, Q₃ = 30, IQR = 10.

Mean = 25, Standard deviation ≈ 4.08 (< 10).

questions.question:
56228. If two independent samples have sizes n1=10 and n2=12, the degrees of freedom for a pooled t-test is:
যদি দুটি স্বাধীন স্যাম্পলের আকার হয় n1=10 এবং n2=12, তাহলে pooled t-test এর জন্য degrees of freedom (df)-স্বাধীনতা মাত্রা হবে:
questions.explain:
For a two-sample t-test assuming equal variances, the degrees of freedom (df) are calculated by adding the sample sizes of the two groups and subtracting 2: df = n₁ + n₂ - 2, where n₁ is the size of the first group and n₂ is the size of the second group.
